newsitem.title: POLAND: Handlowy rises in surging turnover.
newsitem.headline: Handlowy rises in surging turnover.

text.p: Poland's Bank Handlowy SA rose 1.6 percent to 38.5 zlotys in heavy trade and could continue rising gradually toward 40 zlotys before profit-taking falls begin, traders said.
Analysts said Handlowy's 105.9-million-zloty turnover on Tuesday, nearly half the session's main market trade, reflected larger investors taking up shares sold by smaller.
"It seems some small investors who bought at the public offering want to take profits of about 15 percent," one trader said.
Handlowy started trade on Monday 8.3 percent above issue at 37.9 zlotys.

The 9.75-million-share retail tranche of the bank's May-June offering at 35 zlotys each was three times subscribed and the 19.5-million-share institutional tranche was 17.4 times subscribed with foreign demand over $3.5 billion.
The 24-percent long-term investor tranche went to JP Morgan, Zurich Insurance and Swedbank.
Handlowy's Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) currently trade on the London bourse.
Analysts said said some small investors might be selling the bank to buy copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz SA, whose public offering started on Monday.
